## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Rathavinīta Sutta* ("Prepared Chariots", MN 24) is the twenty-fourth discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* [SuttaCentral]. Set initially at the Bamboo Grove in Rājagaha, the narrative centers on an encounter between Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāniputta [SuttaCentral; Shaw 2014]. Sāriputta engages Puṇṇa in a dialogue without initially revealing his identity, asking about the purpose of living the holy life under the Buddha [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Anālayo 2003]. Puṇṇa explains that the spiritual life is lived neither for ethical purity nor mental purity in themselves, but for final Nibbāna without clinging [Anālayo 2003].
To illustrate how each progressive stage supports the next without being the final goal, Puṇṇa introduces the simile of a relay of seven chariots (*rathavinīta*) used by a king to travel to Sāketa [Shankman 2008; Shaw 2014; Anālayo 2003]. He maps this sequence onto seven purifications (*visuddhi*): purification of morality (*sīla*), mind (*citta*), view (*diṭṭhi*), overcoming doubt (*kaṅkhāvitaraṇa*), knowledge and vision of what is and is not the path (*maggāmaggañāṇadassana*), knowledge and vision of the way (*paṭipadāñāṇadassana*), and knowledge and vision (*ñāṇadassana*) [Bond 1988; Crosby 2014]. In the Pali Canon, this exact sevenfold sequence appears elsewhere only in the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 34) within a nine-factored list [Shankman 2008]. It famously became the foundational organizational outline for Ācariya Buddhaghosa's classic Theravāda manual, the *Visuddhimagga* [Bond 1988; Shankman 2008; Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Crosby 2014].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral comprise Chinese translations in the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 9) and the *Ekottara Āgama* (EĀ 39.10), as well as Sanskrit fragments preserved in the Turfan collection (SHT sutta 14) [SuttaCentral; Bingenheimer 2018]. DharmaNexus corroborates these cross-language relationships with strong alignments to MĀ 9 (T 26.9) and EĀ 39.10 (T 125.39.10), while also showing text-reuse matches with the *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the Sanskrit *Nidānasaṃyukta* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 1,755 matching passages across 133 texts, sharing notable textual segments with AN 9, SN 35, AN 4, AN 10, several Vinaya Khandhakas (Kd 6, Kd 1, Kd 8), and its commentary, the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
